correspondence.finding: The selected opening lies on the western edge of a small coastal projection on the southeastern shore of Kings Bay. The first two-position part cuts east across the projection’s tip and then reaches adjacent bay water. The clean map shows coastal land and water, not a river channel through that shortcut. The source position is not treated as a natural headwater.

The second original part turns northeast and then east through shallow nearshore bay water, beside the small stream-mouth and shore setting east of the opening projection. The nearby mapped stream remains a separate incoming component; it does not supply a name for this offshore continuation.
The third part proceeds northeast through open bay water, roughly parallel to the southeastern shoreline. Its shared endpoints connect the adjacent selected parts within the same bay setting.
The fourth part continues northeast and east over bay water beside the southeastern shore. No mapped river reach or lake passage is selected here.

The fifth part makes successive northeast and east steps across bay water beside the Applegate Glacier-side coastal slopes. The glacier and its landward drainage remain outside the selected offshore line and do not name it.
The sixth part continues northeast across the same open-water coastal margin. The mapped shoreline and incoming streams remain southeast of the selected bay passage.

The seventh part turns northeast, east and northeast through the bay, staying on the water side of the southeastern coast near a small glacial-lake outlet setting. All six stored positions and the longer eastward segment are within the ordinary bay/nearshore setting; no transfer through the inland lake is asserted.
The eighth part proceeds northeast over bay water from the nearshore bend toward the bay interior.
The ninth part is the short eastward connection within the same uninterrupted bay-water setting. It retains its original separate part identity.
The tenth part continues northeast through Kings Bay water to the stage3/stage2 fragment join. The join is offshore and does not require an unobserved river, lake outlet or glacier connection.

The first part of the second fragment continues northeast from the shared fragment join through bay water. The change from stage3 to stage2 is retained as stored metadata, not interpreted as a geographic name boundary.
The second part of the second fragment continues northeast across the bay interior; both endpoints and the intervening segment are within connected mapped bay water.
The third part of the second fragment continues northeast through bay water, northwest of the southeastern coastal peninsula.
The fourth part of the second fragment reaches the northernmost selected bend in open bay water. The northern shore remains separate from this selected position.
The fifth part of the second fragment turns east across open bay water north of the southeastern peninsula. Its two stored positions do not follow a mapped river channel.

The sixth part of the second fragment turns southeast and then south in bay water toward the small northern tip of the southeastern peninsula. All three positions remain within the ordinary nearshore approach.

The final part of the second fragment continues south-southeast from bay water to the mapped shoreline of a small projection. The higher-precision render ending and stored quantized ending occupy that same coastal-edge setting. The separately retained source endpoint is offshore to the north-northeast. Neither endpoint is interpreted as a river mouth, surveyed coastline or legal bay boundary.
